description: DASHBOARD (reporting-ui): consume the new per-grade /api/sweep-log shape and rebuild the 'Swept competitions' panel to show PER-GRADE rows GROUPED UNDER each competition (option i) with a per-competition subtotal and an overall grand total. Depends on FEAT-001 (the worker's new field shape). Next.js v16 static export, client-only page.
steps: PREREQUISITE (AGENTS.md): before editing the 'use client' page, read the relevant Next.js v16 guide under reporting-ui/node_modules/next/dist/docs/ (present after npm install). The page must stay a client component with no server routes/handlers/actions and no generateStaticParams (output:'export').

In reporting-ui/lib/api/playerSweep.ts: change the SweepLogEntry type to { seasonId: string; gradeId: string; competitionName: string; organisationName: string; gradeName: string; playerCount: number; lastSweptAt: string }. In getSweepLog() add the new mappings `gradeId: String(r.grade_id ?? '')` and `gradeName: String(r.grade_name ?? '')` alongside the existing seasonId/competitionName/organisationName/playerCount/lastSweptAt mappings. Keep cache:'no-store' and errorFrom. Update the JSDoc to say one entry per swept (season, grade).

In reporting-ui/app/player-sweep/page.tsx, rework the 'Swept competitions' <section> (the grand-total card + the flat table). Keep the sweepLog state, refreshSweepLog(), the mount useEffect, the live refresh after each successful batch and at loop end, and ALL existing preview/sweep/retry-backoff/Stop/cursor behavior UNCHANGED. Derive a grouped view from sweepLog (SweepLogEntry[]) IN RENDER (no new state): group entries by competition keyed on seasonId; group label = `competitionName · organisationName`; group lastSweptAt = max of its entries' lastSweptAt; within a group list each GRADE row (gradeName + its playerCount right-aligned + its lastSweptAt date) sorted by gradeName asc; per-competition SUBTOTAL = sum of that group's grade playerCounts; sort competition groups by most-recent lastSweptAt desc.

Grand total: keep the top emerald number as the sum of ALL grade playerCounts across all groups (sweepLog.reduce((s,e)=>s+e.playerCount,0) — formula unchanged, now summing per-grade rows). Update the header line that says 'Players swept across N competitions' to reflect both counts, e.g. 'across N competitions / M grades' where N = number of groups and M = sweepLog.length. Reword the clarifying caption to state the total sums per-GRADE distinct counts (player-grade memberships; a player in two grades counts in each), NOT globally-distinct people.

Render the grouped data with dark-theme styling consistent with the current panel: reuse the existing border-white/10, bg-white/[0.02], emerald accents, and the <table>/<th> classes. Use a competition sub-header block (or sub-header rows) with its grade rows and a subtotal row underneath; keep it inside an overflow-x-auto wrapper. Empty state (sweepLog.length === 0): 'No competitions swept yet.'
acceptance_criteria: SweepLogEntry includes gradeId and gradeName and getSweepLog() maps grade_id/grade_name from the worker rows.

The 'Swept competitions' panel shows grades grouped under each competition, each grade with its own player count and last-swept date, a per-competition subtotal, and an overall grand total summing all per-grade counts.
The clarifying caption describes per-grade memberships (a player in two grades counts in each), not globally-distinct people.
Empty state reads 'No competitions swept yet.'; live refresh after each batch and at loop end still works; all existing sweep/preview/Stop behavior is unchanged.
The page remains a client-only component valid under Next.js v16 output:'export' (no server routes/handlers/actions, no generateStaticParams).
verification: From c:\Users\AndyDin\reporting-dashboard\.worktrees\sweep-log-grade\reporting-ui: run `npm install` if node_modules is absent.
Run `npx tsc --noEmit` — expect no type errors.

Run `npm run build` — expect the static export to succeed. KNOWN QUIRK: a prerender failure isolated to the /fixtures route is a pre-existing env-gap (not a regression) as long as /player-sweep builds.
